newsitem.title: USA: EPA gives $500,000 to New Hampshire for cleanup.
newsitem.headline: EPA gives $500,000 to New Hampshire for cleanup.

text.p: Environmental Protection Agency grants of $500,000 earmarked for 11 statewide programs will prevent pollution, encourage sustainable forest practices and spur economic growth, John DeVillars, administrator of the agency's New England Office, said Friday.

"These grant dollars will go a long way to protect, preserve and promote New Hampshire's environment," DeVillars said just before setting out on a tour of Concord's blighted industrial corridor, an abandoned, heavily polluted 440 acre tract, eyed for cleanup and revitalization by the city.

Concord was awarded $90,000 of the grant to identify and plan restoration of more than 60 suspected contaminated sites in the corridor. Mayor William Veroneau told DeVillars at a city hall news conference that the grant is the first step in a multimillion dollar rebirth of the polluted zone.

Londonderry officials also received $50,000 from EPA to help the town foreclose on a formerly contaminated parcel so a new company can move in. Both communities say their so-called "brownfields" programs will provide prime real estate sites for prospective business and industry within a few years.
A $69,122 grant was provided for a pilot program which collects and recycles electronic components, computers and other equipment from consumers in Somerville, Mass., and Binghamton, N.Y.

Other EPA grants included $55,000 for University of New Hampshire to establish a pilot program for small metal finishing companies that need help complying with air and solid waste pollution laws and $26,000 for a forestry program encouraging sustainable timber harvesting.
